summary: On paper the Rams have the edge (The Rams' defense ranks 12th in EPA per dropback with motion, +0.08 allowed), while Denver's best counter is to move people pre-snap (Denver ranks 8th in EPA per dropback with motion, +0.11). The model favors the Rams at 57%, mostly on rushing matchup (2.4 pts) and starting QB (1.8 pts).

LA.detail: The Rams' defense ranks 12th in EPA per dropback with motion (+0.08 allowed). Denver ranks 8th (+0.11).

DEN.detail: Denver ranks 8th in EPA per dropback with motion (+0.11). The Rams' defense ranks 12th (+0.08 allowed).

team_cards.t1: Denver has the 8th-best motion passing game.
team_cards.t2: The Rams' defense vs motion ranks 12th.
team_cards.source: NFLVERSE PLAY-BY-PLAY · FTN CHARTING VIA NFLVERSE
team_cards.note: Garbage time removed · DEN: n=26 dropbacks

model.summary: Model: the Rams 57% to win, fair line LA -2. Market: Denver 50%. The largest factor is rushing matchup, worth 2.4 points toward the Rams.

model_cards.t1: The model likes the Rams more than the market.
model_cards.sub: Win probability. Market = vig-free moneyline at build time.
model_cards.source: NFLVERSE PLAY-BY-PLAY · INJURIES · SNAP COUNTS · SCHEDULES (LINES)
model_cards.note: Not betting advice · market line at build time

model_cards.sub: Each factor's push on the projected margin, in points. Positive = toward Denver. Sum = LA -2.
model_cards.source: NFLVERSE PLAY-BY-PLAY · INJURIES · SNAP COUNTS · SCHEDULES (LINES)
model_cards.note: Linear model, so contributions are exact SHAP values · vs. an average matchup

model_cards.sub: Distribution of Denver's margin. Shaded area = Denver win (43%).
model_cards.source: NFLVERSE PLAY-BY-PLAY · INJURIES · SNAP COUNTS · SCHEDULES (LINES)
model_cards.note: Normal margin, sigma = 12.0 points (fit by log loss)

model_cards.t1: The Rams are missing 1.5 starters' worth of snaps.
model_cards.t2: Injuries move the line 0.9 points toward Denver.

model_cards.t1: The biggest unit gap: the Rams' pass offense.
